newsitem.title: UK: ROWING-REDGRAVE TO GO FOR FIFTH OLYMPIC GOLD. [CORRECTED 15:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: ROWING-REDGRAVE TO GO FOR FIFTH OLYMPIC GOLD. [CORRECTED 15:10 GMT]

text.p: Steve Redgrave has reversed his decision to quit rowing and has set his sights on an unprecedented fifth gold medal at the Sydney Olympics.
"If anyone sees me near a boat they can shoot me, " he had vowed after clinching victory with partner Matthew Pinsent in the coxless pairs in Atlanta.

But at a news conference on Thursday Redgrave admitted that the pull of competition and the chance to strike gold at five successive Games had proved too great (Corrects to delete reference to Redgrave becoming the first Olympic competitor to win gold medals at five successive Games.)
"My heart really lies with the competition," said Redgrave who plans to form a four with Pinsent.
"Both Matthew and I did not really want to carry on as a pair as we have done for the past six years.
"If I had to put it put it down to anything it was the desire to go to another Olympics. I still feel I am young enough to carry on."
He said he had declined several very tempting coaching offers during his four months hiatus from the sport.
While the thought of further Olympic glory is Redgrave's biggest spur, he and Pinsent -- Britain's only gold medallists in Atlanta -- have also received a huge financial carrot.
A finance firm will back the pair in a one million pound ($1.6 million) deal over the next four years, the biggest sponsorship in the history of British rowing.
